name: Downtown and the Old City Quarter
tagline: The harbour front and the heritage blocks above it
description: The centre around the harbour, with the seaplane dock, the passenger ferry terminal, the Bastion and the Old City Quarter's heritage buildings on the slope behind. It is the only walkable part of Nanaimo and where the coworking and most of the bars are.
bestFor: Anyone working without a car or commuting to Vancouver by air
pros: Float plane and passenger ferry at the door
Harbour views and the seawall walk
cons: Visible homelessness and property crime downtown
Limited grocery shopping in the core

name: Departure Bay
tagline: The ferry terminal side with the best city beach
description: The bay north of downtown with the BC Ferries terminal to Horseshoe Bay at one end and a long sandy beach along the front. Residential streets rise behind it, and it is the most pleasant part of the city to be based in for anyone crossing to the mainland often.
bestFor: Anyone using the mainland ferry regularly
pros: Ferry to Horseshoe Bay at the door
The best swimming beach in the city
cons: Ferry traffic on the main roads at sailing times

name: North Nanaimo
tagline: The newer suburbs with the shopping and the ocean views
description: The area spreading north along the highway, with the newest housing, the main shopping centres and streets that look out across the Strait of Georgia to the mainland mountains. It is where most of the people who moved here from Vancouver ended up.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting new-build housing and a view
pros: Newest housing stock and best internet
Ocean and mountain views from many streets
All the major shopping is here

name: Harewood
tagline: The university side, cheapest and closest to the trails
description: The neighbourhood immediately south of downtown around Vancouver Island University, with older houses, student rentals and the best access to the Colliery Dam park and the trails up towards Mount Benson. Rents are the lowest in the city.
bestFor: Budget stays and anyone who wants trail access on foot
pros: Colliery Dam park and Mount Benson trails
Walking distance to downtown and the university
cons: Older housing stock in variable condition
Few shops or cafes in the area

name: Cedar and South Nanaimo
tagline: Semi-rural acreage south of the city
description: The countryside south towards the Duke Point ferry, with small farms, wineries, acreage properties and the Cedar village centre. It is greener, quieter and cheaper per square metre than the city, and the Tsawwassen ferry terminal is at its southern edge.
bestFor: Anyone with a vehicle wanting land and quiet
pros: Duke Point ferry to Tsawwassen nearby
Cheaper per square metre than the city
